purpose: Frozen run-local rules for cohort support adjudication and comparability. These rules do not rewrite metric-shard measurements; they make support classification and its evidence mechanically consistent.

rules.rule: A wrapper, scalar type, foreign-function helper, or other mechanism that is documented in the language's normal standard runtime/library and ships with the frozen toolchain is not third-party merely because it is a wrapper. If it delivers some but not every numbered sub-requirement, classify it PARTIAL under P-a when applicable rather than NONE solely because the language lacks a native primitive.

When the same documented mechanism is used on multiple probes, classify that mechanism under the same rubric logic. Probe-specific numbered requirements may still produce different levels, but the adjudication must state the concrete numbered requirement that distinguishes them.

For FFI, distinguish a flag/mode or automatic compiler invocation that ships inside the frozen toolchain from a separate build system, external binding generator, third-party package, hand-written glue artifact, or toolchain outside the frozen environment. The former may be FULL or P-b depending on the exact frozen recipe; the latter is NONE under the applicable N-reason. State the distinguishing frozen-recipe fact explicitly.

Do not change FULL/PARTIAL/NONE for determinacy, locality, elegance, or hidden semantics that the frozen probe marks as an observation target. Those belong to the separate Semantic Compression quality metrics.

cross_probe_checks.rule: Fixed-width numeric wrapper/substitution mechanisms must be classified consistently under standard-library-mechanisms-are-standard and same-mechanism-same-rubric.
